about: Known differences planted in copies of openai/math comparator statements, to measure whether a statement audit notices them. Each `old` must occur exactly once in the challenge's statement file. All but `placement-reversed` weaken a proven statement, so a proof of the planted version would still exist: those are the differences a Lean check can never catch.

FiniteCongruenceGraph.what: Only one direction of the paper's 'if and only if': a graph witness gives a representation, but not the converse.
Admissible placements must raise edge colours where the paper's lower them: d(p,q) ≤ d(f(p),f(q)) instead of d(f(p),f(q)) ≤ d(p,q).
FiniteCongruenceGraph.old: ∀ left right, color (placement left) (placement right) ≤ color left right
FiniteCongruenceGraph.new: ∀ left right, color left right ≤ color (placement left) (placement right)

FourRowPermanent.what: Allows p₀ = 2, where the inequality was already known; the paper's point is an exponent strictly below two.
Row norms drop the paper's 1/4 normalization, which enlarges the right-hand side and weakens the inequality. The file's own comment still says the norms are normalized.

PlaneColoring.what: Colours the real line, not the plane.
Only points within distance 100 of the origin need different colours at distance one.
PlaneColoring.old: ∀ x y : Plane, dist x y = 1 → c x ≠ c y
PlaneColoring.new: ∀ x y : Plane, ‖x‖ ≤ 100 → ‖y‖ ≤ 100 → dist x y = 1 → c x ≠ c y
